name: napari
raw_meta_yaml:
context:
  name: napari
  version: "0.9.1"
  python_min: "3.11"
  build_number: 0

recipe:
  name: ${{ name|lower }}
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  - url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/${{ name[0] }}/${{ name }}/${{ name }}-${{ version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: 9a0712de1ede928e1274cec7c0d04a263eaec8be76e231435d99f988cfe51a98
  - url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/napari/napari/v${{ version }}/resources/conda_menu_config.json
    target_directory: resources
    sha256: 61a9907bb60eb07d5b00f27df709f8b790deb7f2247e46e9928ecd8b473d831f

build:
  number: ${{ build_number }}

outputs:
  - package:
      name: napari-base
    build:
      noarch: python
      script: python -m pip install . -vv
      python:
        entry_points:
          - napari = napari.__main__:main
    requirements:
      host:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        - pip
        - setuptools >=77.0.1
        - setuptools_scm >=8
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}

        # dependencies matched to pyproject.toml
        - app-model >=0.5.0,<0.6.0a
        - cachey >=0.2.1
        - certifi >=2018.1.18
        # Do not depend on base "dask" package since it pulls
        # in the distributed dependency
        # conda-forge doesn't have the dask-array subpackage
        # so depend on cytoolz and numpy manually
        - cytoolz >=0.11.0
        - dask-core >=2022.1.1
        - imageio >=2.20,!=2.22.1
        - jsonschema >=3.2.0
        - lazy_loader >=0.3
        - magicgui >=0.7.0
        - napari-console >=0.1.4
        - napari-plugin-engine >=0.2.1
        - napari-svg >=0.1.8
        - npe2 >=0.8.1
        - numpy >=1.25.0
        - pandas >=1.5.0
        - pillow >=10.0
        - pint >=0.17
        - platformdirs >=4.3.0
        - psutil >=5.9.0
        - psygnal >=0.14.2
        - pydantic >=2.8.0
        - pygments >=2.13.0
        - pydantic-extra-types
        - pydantic-settings
        - pyopengl >=3.1.10
        - pywin32 >=302 # only needed for windows, but helps keep the package noarch
        - pyyaml >=6.0
        - qtpy >=2.4.0
        - scikit-image >=0.20.0
        - scipy >=1.14.0
        - superqt >=0.7.8
        - tifffile >=2022.7.28
        - toolz >=0.12.1
        - tqdm >=4.56.0
        - typing_extensions >=4.12
        - vispy >=0.16.2,<0.17.0a0
        - wrapt >=1.14.1
      run_constraints:
        - pyside6 >=6.7.1,!=6.11.0,!=6.11.1  # see: napari/napari#9054
        - pyqt >=5.15.8,<6.0a0
        - pyqt6 >=6.5,!=6.6.1,!=6.11.0,!=6.11.1  # see: napari/napari#9054
    tests:
      - python:
          pip_check: true
          imports:
            - napari
          python_version:
            - ${{ python_min }}.*
            - "*"

      - script:
          - ${{ 'setx QT_API pyqt6' if win else 'export QT_API=pyqt6' }}
          - ${{ 'where napari' if win else 'which napari' }}
          - if: linux
            then: 'QT_XCB_GL_INTEGRATION=none QT_DEBUG_PLUGINS=1 LIBGL_DEBUG=verbose xvfb-run --auto-servernum napari --info | grep -C99 "napari: ${PKG_VERSION}"'
            else:
              - napari --info
          # - pytest --pyargs napari
        requirements:
          run:
            - pyqt6
            # needed if pytest is uncommented above in 'script'
            #   - hypothesis
            #   - pytest
            #   - pytest-faulthandler
            #   - pytest-qt
            #   - xarray
            #   - pandas
            #   - pytest-timeout
    about:
      homepage: http://napari.org
      summary: a fast n-dimensional image viewer in Python, with only the required dependencies
      license: BSD-3-Clause AND MIT
      license_file:
        - LICENSE
        - src/napari/_vendor/qt_json_builder/LICENSE
      documentation: http://napari.org
      repository: https://github.com/napari/napari

  - package:
      name: napari
    build:
      noarch: python
    requirements:
      host:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('napari-base', exact=True) }}
        - aiohttp  # needed to open remote files by zarr
        - bermuda >=0.1.5
        - fsspec
        - napari-metadata >=0.1.1
        - napari-plugin-manager >=0.1.10,<0.2.0a0
        - numba >=0.58.0
        - partsegcore-compiled-backend >=0.15.11
        - pooch >=1.6.0
        - zarr >=3.0.8
    tests:  # just to check that the environment can indeed solve
      - requirements:
          run:
            - python ${{ python_min }}.*
            - pyside6  # use this opportunity to test solvability with other backend
        script:
          - python -c "from napari import Viewer"
    about:
      homepage: http://napari.org
      summary: a fast n-dimensional image viewer in Python
      license: BSD-3-Clause AND MIT
      license_file:
        - LICENSE
      documentation: http://napari.org
      repository: https://github.com/napari/napari

  - package:
      name: napari-menu
    build:
      noarch: python
      script:
        - mkdir -p "${{ PREFIX }}/Menu"
        - sed "s/__PKG_VERSION__/${{ PKG_VERSION }}/" "${{ SRC_DIR }}/resources/conda_menu_config.json" > "${{ PREFIX }}/Menu/napari-menu.json"
        - |
          # Download and extract icons from latest napari/resources release
          mkdir -p /tmp/napari-icons
          curl -sL https://github.com/napari/resources/releases/latest/download/icons.tar.gz | tar xz -C /tmp/napari-icons
          cp /tmp/napari-icons/artifacts/icons/gradient-plain-light.png "${{ PREFIX }}/Menu/napari.png"
          cp /tmp/napari-icons/artifacts/icons/gradient-padded-light.icns "${{ PREFIX }}/Menu/napari.icns"
          cp /tmp/napari-icons/artifacts/icons/gradient-plain-light.ico "${{ PREFIX }}/Menu/napari.ico"
    requirements:
      build:
        - if: unix
          then:
            - sed
          else:
            - m2-sed
      host:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('napari', exact=True) }}
    tests:
      - requirements:
          run:
            - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        script:
          - python -c "import napari"
      - package_contents:
          files:
            - Menu/napari-menu.json
    about:
      homepage: http://napari.org
      summary: Shortcut to open napari from the desktop environment menus
      license: BSD-3-Clause AND MIT
      license_file:
        - LICENSE
      documentation: http://napari.org
      repository: https://github.com/napari/napari

about:
  homepage: http://napari.org
  summary: a fast n-dimensional image viewer in Python
  license: BSD-3-Clause AND MIT
  license_file:
    - LICENSE
